samples.summary: The new comment's rationale is factually wrong about its siblings: it says "Same reason every sibling mutation below notifies", but `toggleList` (editor.ts:2885), `indent` (2904) and `outdent` still omit `notifyStyleApplied()`. The task doc repeats the same claim (docs/tasks/active/20260817-block-type-toolbar-refresh-todo.md:16-18, "`setBlockType` is the only outlier"). The one-line fix itself is the right shape and matches the issue scope; only the justifying comment/spec text is inaccurate, so a future reader will trust a pattern that does not hold.

Under-fix relative to the issue's outcome: the stale Text-style/toolbar class of bug survives on the other toolbar-driven block-type entry points (`toggleList`, `indent`, `outdent`), which also change `getBlockType()` output (list kind/level) without firing the cursor-move callbacks. The task's Non-goals explicitly exclude "Any other toolbar control or block-type entry point", so this is sanctioned narrowing rather than a criterion failure — flagged so the panel can decide whether the issue's outcome is really met for list buttons.

The lessons file asserts "ending an EditorAPI mutation with `notifyStyleApplied()` is part of the contract", but no design doc under docs/design/ records that contract (grep for `notifyStyleApplied` in docs/design returns nothing). Not required by CONTRIBUTING for a one-line bug fix — no architecture or data-model change here — so this is a taste-level suggestion to fold one sentence into the canonical Docs subsystem doc rather than leaving it only in a task lessons file.
